results: Not settled. The preregistered sequence did not run on a disposable store: after `init`, every subcommand reached the live service on 127.0.0.1:49374 and operated on the live store, a known hazard whose fix (own port plus AI_MEMORY_SERVER_URL) was already recorded in deletion-erasure-probe.json and visible in this run's own init output. Nothing new about TTL or erasure was learned relative to the prior deletion-erasure-probe: (1) TTL was not exercised; the CLI write-page lacks --expires-at, but the MCP/HTTP memory_write_page tool accepts expires_at (this project's AGENTS.md: 'For time-bounded memory, set expires_at'), so a disposable serve could have exercised it; (2) the backup contained the token (zgrep matched) only because it was taken while the page was live, and it was shredded without a post-deletion check; (3) `compact --confirm` ran before `purge-project`, so the run says nothing about compact-based erasure; (4) the post-hoc `grep -c ttl-probe` = 13 counts lines holding the page path, not the marker token. What the raw output does show: the full page body with the literal token is committed in the live wiki's git history (bb0b205, `git show` output), unaffected by the purge commit 4be633d. The live store was mutated (a page write and purge, a VACUUM of the 223.7 MiB database, a 130 MiB backup of live content written and then shredded). This is an unremediated isolation breach that needs an operator decision; see the layer README.
limits: Ran against the live store by accident; not a controlled experiment and not evidence for the TTL/erasure protocol.
TTL not exercised: the CLI lacks --expires-at, but MCP/HTTP memory_write_page accepts expires_at on a disposable serve.
Token residue in the live database file is unmeasured (the grep counted a path substring); token residue in the live wiki git history (bb0b205) is shown by git show.

Remaining: the whole next_check on a disposable instance (own loopback port, AI_MEMORY_SERVER_URL exported, ideally inside unshare -rn): write a token page with expires_at via MCP/HTTP, forget-sweep, backup, compact --confirm, then `grep -a -o TOKEN | wc -l` over wiki, wiki/.git, sqlite, WAL and the backup archive.

Fix-round read-only follow-ups also contacted the live store: grep and git log/show on its files, and `ai-memory status` CLI calls to the live service (transcript calls [7], [13], [50]). They changed nothing recorded, but the status calls break the ai-memory isolation rule.
